summary:
tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 no longer hard-codes the Facts, twinned-entry or pattern counts. Get-RuleCounts recounts them from the tree's own yaml and .cs, and every expectation is that recount plus an offset. On the real tree the recount gives 11/15/27 and parity gives 11/15/27/49 under both hosts. C-001 to C-005 exit 0 under powershell.exe and under pwsh.

**Historical states.** To go beyond the builder's own scratch fixtures, I replayed 14 real states of this repo's rule files, from SL-031 to a9e0d1d, under HEAD's RuleCases.ps1 and rules-parity.ps1. The parity tool is unchanged since 867092c.
- Those states cover 7/10/21, 8/11/23 and 11/15/27, with settled counts from 7 to 47.
- The fixed C-001 held on every one. On both sides of SL-043's real transition (8/11/23/21 to 11/15/27/24, which includes two-scope splits), C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005 all held.
- The pre-fix script failed C-001 with 6 checks on each of the 7 states whose counts differ from 11/15/27. So the replay does exercise the bug.

**My own runs, all exit 0:**
- Sibling test `-Shape All` (513 s, 177 ok, 0 FAIL).
- `-Shape EngineCases` with the real engine and dotnet (316 s). C-007 and C-008 held on this tree and on a two-scope copy (12/17/28); the delete case expected Twinned-1 and got it.
- SettledCountProbe `Misclassified` and `GuardRule`.
- Fitness op=check: 64 rules hold.

**Mutation checks:**
- A read-back version of Get-RuleCounts turns the Misclassified probe red (exit 1): C-001 then passes on a miscounting tool.
- A data-driven [Theory] makes both parity and the harness exit 2 (CANNOT-READ), so it fails loudly.
- Literals planted in a scratch copy are caught by the engine's own fitness.check, except the argument-array `-ExpectFacts` spelling.

**Two review fixes owed to build-slice are still not in the tree:**
- O-024: the argument-array `-ExpectFacts` spelling is not guarded.
- O-025: harness.py:575 still prints the Python list repr, and RuleCases.ps1:685 still uses `.Trim("'")`.

Neither blocks a criterion today: the only must_not_import rule has no apostrophe, and a re-pinned C-005 value still fails through its derived message. The engine should route them back to build-slice.

**Temp folders.** %TEMP% holds leftover folders created 12:04 to 12:32 today: 155 fsa-parity-case-*, 6 fsa-sl069-* and 2 fsa-rules-*. Their yamls are changed copies. Normal runs of RuleCases C-003, C-004 and C-005 and of sibling SingleScope measured 0 left behind, so the leftovers are most likely from runs killed before cleanup. I could not tie them to a process and did not delete them.

**Build attempts.** The three attempts are not a loop: the first hit a provider limit, the second was partial, and the third fixed the harness.

**Thin bug report.** Nothing beyond the title was written down, so I took the repro, the design's 14 cases and the slice's two statements as the acceptance. No block titled 'What this slice owes' was shown, so `planned` is empty, and the design's 14 numbered cases are graded under `criteria`.

Fixed C-001 held on 14 real historical states from 7/10/21 to 11/15/27, where the pre-fix script failed on every state not at 11/15/27. The read-back mutant turns the Misclassified probe red, so the recount is independent of the tool.

criteria.how: The design owed no test ('fails loudly'). Measured: [Theory] plus [InlineData] rows make parity exit 2 CANNOT-READ, C-001 exit 1, and the harness C-007 invokes exit 2 before any trx. C-007 itself was not run on that tree.

criteria.criterion: Assumed acceptance (the bug report is a title only): C-001..C-005 green on the clean tree under both hosts; SettledCountProbe Misclassified and GuardRule exit 0
criteria.how: 10 RuleCases runs all exit 0. Both probe shapes exit 0.

obligations.evidence: The recount moved with every addition I fed in: SingleScope 12/16/28 (twice), TwoScope/HostParity 12/17/28, EngineCases copy 12/17/28 with C-008 at 12/16/28. It also moved with real history: SL-040 7/10/21 to 8/11/23 and SL-043 8/11/23 to 11/15/27. C-001 held on every state; the repro exit 0 is on record (O-001).
SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified exit 0 on this tree (C-001 fails with 4 checks on the stub, both shells). A read-back Get-RuleCounts mutant makes that probe exit 1.

The loose regex '^\s*\[\s*(Fact|Theory)\b' gives 11 on the clean ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, the same as the strict '^\s*\[(Fact|Theory)\]\s*$'. The only other 'Theory' text is inside a pattern literal at :79 and does not start a line with '['.

$Repo = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot) (RuleCases.ps1:25). The recount reads only $CsRel and $YamlRel, and the repro copies both plus RuleCases and parity. Measured: scratch copies of real 7/10/21/7 and 8/11/23/21 trees made C-001 expect exactly those counts, not the worktree's.

Still unfixed in the tree. No `-ExpectFacts['"]?\s*,\s*['"]?\d` in fitness.yaml, and the engine's fitness.check did not hit a planted `@('-ExpectFacts', '11')` line. Owed to build-slice, not to this stage. It did not block any criterion: a re-pinned C-005 value still fails through its derived message and exit code.

Still unfixed: harness.py:575 prints `{names}` (Python repr), and RuleCases.ps1:685 still uses `.Trim().Trim("'")`. Owed to build-slice. Latent today: the only must_not_import rule has no apostrophe, and C-007 held with the engine.

not_reached: A real future slice declaring a twinned rule through the engine's own flow. Only scratch-copy simulations and replays of this repo's past rule states were run.
C-007 itself on a tree with a data-driven [Theory]. I ran the parity tool, C-001 and the harness command C-007 invokes (all fail loudly), but not the C-007 case.
O-025's failure shape (a must_not_import rule whose name has an apostrophe) was not exercised; no such rule exists yet.

Who created the 155 fsa-parity-case-*, 6 fsa-sl069-* and 2 fsa-rules-* folders in %TEMP% dated 12:04-12:32 today. Normal completion measured 0 left behind, so they are probably from killed runs. They were left in place.
The acceptance repro was not re-run here by design; its exit 0 is the engine's measurement (O-001).
